newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate up on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate up on profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates was up 140 basis points in early trade at 17.90 percent in early trade on Thursday.
Analysts said rates had risen on profit-taking after a late dip on Wednesday, but they expected levels to ease down later on a strong peso and lower U.S. long bond yields.
"U.S. consumer prices data suggest long bond yields will not rise, and that will take upside pressure off domestic rates," a fixed-income analyst said.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was up 20/32 to yield 6.58 percent.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were meanwhile 0.95 percent firmer at 7.7675/7.7695 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper were up 10 basis points at 18.70 percent.

Liquidity of 2.388 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation. Dealers estimated an additional 1.5 billion pesos in cash could flow back into the market.
